Alright, I've just applied a series of patches: extended the S bridge in the maps, fixed the weapon view‑model rendering, adjusted the HUD anchoring for the new first‑person sprites, exported the map metadata, and rendered all four dioramas (vector, foundry, canopy, bastion). The validation script for the bastion map now reports “BASTION OK”, and the diorama render step completed without errors. I also updated the playtest script (playtest.mjs) to use simulation‑time based bot movement checks instead of wall‑clock waits, which should make the test more reliable across different environments.

At this point the only thing left is to verify that the entire game pipeline works end‑to‑end with the latest changes. The playtest.mjs script contains a suite of checks (bot navigation, map loading, HUD rendering, etc.) and prints either “✘” for failures or “checks passed” for successes. Running the script directly with Node will execute all the tests, but the console output is verbose. To focus on the relevant results, I should pipe the output through grep, filtering for lines that contain either the failure marker (✘) or the success phrase (“checks passed”). That way I’ll get a concise summary of any problems.

I also need to make sure the command runs long enough, since the full suite includes loading all maps and rendering dioramas, which can take a while. Setting a generous timeout (10 minutes) will prevent premature termination. Using `2>&1` ensures that both stdout and stderr are captured by grep.

Therefore, the next logical step is to invoke Node on the updated playtest.mjs and filter its output for the key result lines. This will give me a quick, clear view of whether any of the recent fixes introduced regressions.

Command: `node playtest.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E '✘|checks passed'` with a 600 000 ms timeout.

arguments.description: Full playtest with bastion + all fixes
